title: Watch Out Your Album! On the Inadvertent Privacy Memorization in Multi-Modal Large Language Models

problems.title: Binary username-set probe does not identify hidden user-ID association
problems.check: Constructive visible-name-only linear probe and all120 synthetic seen-ID permutations
problems.result: 100% membership accuracy is invariant to all ID assignments; no ID information required
counterevidence: Higher post-tuning accuracy supports representation change
Actual association memory not ruled out
problems.impact: Unsupported specific hidden-association/multi-hop inference; narrower membership evidence survives
problems.correction: Association-specific counterfactual controls needed; not executed

independent_check.source_fidelity: Read source Section 2/3 definitions and physical p.6 Scenario II conclusion; freshly viewed pp.7-8 Figures 4-6 and the explicit binary endpoint, plus p.15 fixed ten synthetic usernames in two sets. Static analyze.py targets/split checked against frozen source hashes.
independent_check.operative_assumptions: Probe images show one of ten fixed usernames, split into two fixed five-name sets; labels classify the set, not the paired ID. Image-level train/test splitting repeats the same underlying names. The countermodel concerns identifiability from this endpoint, not actual representation form.
independent_check.independent_reasoning: A representation e_j read from visible name j and a signed linear weight separates the two sets perfectly. Permuting the five seen ID values leaves every representation, binary label and prediction unchanged; fresh enumeration of all 120 assignments yields binary accuracy 1 and average arbitrary pairing recovery 1/5. Thus the binary endpoint cannot distinguish exact ID association from name recognition or membership.
independent_check.counterevidence_and_alternatives: The 85.5/82.0 pre-tuning and higher post-tuning probe results support representation/separability changes, not identification of which paired ID was retained. Zero direct ID-answer accuracy neither proves absence of latent associations nor supplies independent positive association evidence.
independent_check.dependency_and_severity: Retain Major for the specific hidden username-ID/multi-hop conclusion in RQ2; narrower sensitivity and set-membership evidence survives.
independent_check.repair_scope: Need assignment-sensitive evaluations and pairing-exposure controls while matching visible-name exposure. These are proposed experiments, not executed repairs. Code-paper protocol differences and token-index ambiguity remain bounded reproducibility limits.

problems.title: Covariance probability proof and zero-mean gradient premise do not establish mechanism
problems.check: Exact projection variance/fourth moment; repaired lower-bound proof; four-case independent-sign gradient
problems.result: Chebyshev upper bound cannot imply lower bound; population residual gradient may be nonzero even during nuisance suppression
counterevidence: Gaussian small-sample covariance phenomenon can be locally proved
Observed gradient and representation changes remain descriptive evidence
problems.impact: Invalid supporting derivation for proposed memorization mechanism, not disproof of memorization
problems.correction: Local Gaussian fluctuation result repaired; causal link to persistent memory unverified

independent_check.source_fidelity: Freshly viewed Appendix A pp.14-15 Eqs.(6)-(10); read Section 2 Eq.(3) and the zero full-distribution residual-gradient assertion on p.3, plus p.2 independence of u from both x and y.
independent_check.operative_assumptions: Covariance repair uses iid paired observations, independent Gaussian scalar coordinates, positive variances and B>1; projection rank m=B-1. Gradient counterexample sets original x=0 constant, y,u independent uniform signs, squared loss and arbitrary theta=1. Thus u is independent of both x and y and p(y|x,u)=p(y|x).
independent_check.independent_reasoning: For S=y^T P u/m, variance is sigma_y^2 sigma_u^2 tr(P^2)/m^2 = sigma_y^2 sigma_u^2/m. Centered-product variance has factor (1-1/B)^2. Chebyshev remains only an upper bound; the stated lower-probability consequence is not implied. Fresh exact projection/moment calculations agree with E[S^4]=3(m+2)/m^3, yielding the repaired bound (1-theta)^2 m/[3(m+2)] via Cauchy-Schwarz. Separately, the four residual gradients theta-yu at theta=1 are 0,2,2,0, with mean 1; the original-input gradient is identically zero. Population gradient descent reduces theta and suppresses the nuisance.
independent_check.counterevidence_and_alternatives: The qualitative Gaussian covariance-fluctuation phenomenon is true under nondegeneracy and locally repaired here. An extra optimum/orthogonality premise might force a zero residual mean in a special model, but no such premise is supplied for Eq.(3). Neither covariance nor a gradient change identifies persistent content retention.
independent_check.dependency_and_severity: Major for the supporting derivation of the proposed task-irrelevant memorization mechanism. The report does not refute all mini-batch correlations, measured gradients or actual MLLM memorization.
independent_check.repair_scope: The valid lower bound concerns one Gaussian covariance entry only. Model/loss analysis or controlled pairing-sensitive measurements remain necessary to connect it to persistent memory.

repair_verification: Synthetic countermodels and local Gaussian proof verified; model-level controls not run
